findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance oracle to the avians credential child (9015) that asserts the per-client PAT SSM parameter(s) are committed to the terraform-managed rebar_secret_params set in ssm.tf (as-code / teardownable), covering the parent AC4 'as-code in ssm.tf' sub-clause.
evidence: Parent AC4: 'Per-client bearer PATs are SSM-materialized (as-code in ssm.tf) + gitignored (avians)'
Parent decomposition item 4: 'the SSM parameter is added to the terraform-managed rebar_secret_params set in ssm.tf — reproducible/teardownable as-code'
9015 description prose: 'Terraform SSM params for the per-client PATs ... under the existing /rebar/prod/ prefix; fetch-secrets.sh wiring to materialize them on the box.'
9015 ACs are guard / materialize / verifier / runbook only — none names ssm.tf or rebar_secret_params or asserts the terraform param is committed as-code.
findings.finding: Parent AC4's terraform-as-code sub-clause — 'Per-client bearer PATs are SSM-materialized (as-code in ssm.tf)', elaborated by decomposition item 4 as 'the SSM parameter is added to the terraform-managed rebar_secret_params set in ssm.tf — reproducible/teardownable-as-code' — is not delivered by any sibling's acceptance criteria. The avians child (9015) that owns the credential slice tests only the .gitignore guard, fetch-secrets.sh materialization, and verifier contrast; none of its ACs assert the ssm.tf / rebar_secret_params terraform change is committed. Its prose mentions 'Terraform SSM params ... under the existing /rebar/prod/ prefix' but no AC oracle verifies it.
scenarios: An operator tears down and re-applies terraform expecting the per-client PAT SSM params to be reproducible-as-code, but the param was created out-of-band because no AC forced it into ssm.tf.
Reviewer checks parent AC4 'as-code in ssm.tf' and finds no gated oracle that the ssm.tf change landed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC to 9015 verifying `ssm.tf` declares the per-client PAT params in `rebar_secret_params` (e.g., a terraform plan/parse or grep oracle over ssm.tf), matching the parent's 'as-code in ssm.tf / reproducible-teardownable' wording.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign explicit ownership for setting REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID and REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY (+ the opcert-ed25519-key /run/secrets mount) on the mcp compose service — add it to esok's (fd4a) scope/ACs (or b173's) so b173's signing round-trip and foxterrier's REBAR_OPCERT_* compose-parity oracle have a real source.
evidence: b173: 'esok already landed, on the mcp compose service, REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID=9f1c8e42-... (the cert principal) and REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key'
foxterrier compose-parity oracle: 'mcp_run_new reproduces the compose mcp: service EXACTLY — ... every REBAR_MCP_*/REBAR_OPCERT_* var with compose's literal ${VAR:-default} values'
fd4a (esok) Scope env list: only 'REBAR_MCP_TRANSPORT=http, REBAR_MCP_HTTP_HOST, ...REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STATIC_TOKENS_FILE' — no REBAR_OPCERT_* / REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY
findings.finding: Conflicting assumption / owned-by-none gap on the mcp compose service's opcert env vars. Child b173 (goose) asserts 'esok already landed, on the mcp compose service, REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID=9f1c8e42-... and REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key', and foxterrier's compose-parity oracle pins 'every REBAR_MCP_*/REBAR_OPCERT_* var' as present on the mcp service — but esok's (fd4a) scope and ACs enumerate ONLY REBAR_MCP_* env keys and never mention REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID or REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY. No child's acceptance criteria own placing the opcert env vars on the mcp compose service.
scenarios: b173's move-1 signing round-trip assumes the compose mcp service carries REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID + the signing-key mount, but esok never adds them, so the container signs under the wrong (genesis) key or fails to resolve the principal — exactly the failure b173 warns about.
foxterrier's compose-parity test iterates REBAR_OPCERT_* keys that esok's compose service does not define, so the parity oracle has nothing to pin (or drifts).
findings.suggested_fix: Amend esok (fd4a) scope + an AC to declare REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID=9f1c8e42-... and REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY on the mcp compose service (and the opcert key bind-mount), so b173 can truthfully depend on it and foxterrier's REBAR_OPCERT_* parity assertion is grounded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the observability contract for the new `mcp` prod service: a health/liveness alarm (or log-metric) and its alert destination/owner, consistent with the repo's per-service monitoring_*.tf convention — distinct from the retained-release retention/cap/alert.
evidence: esok scope defines /health with an in_flight gauge that 'feeds foxterrier's retire check; it does not gate the deploy' — a health gauge, not an alarm
The design summary's only alert mention is 'retire-when-idle with retention/cap/alert' — bounded to retained releases, not mcp service liveness
Repo convention: infra/terraform has monitoring_foxterrier.tf, monitoring_autodeploy.tf and other per-service monitoring_*.tf files, none of which the plan extends for the mcp service
ABSENCE: no plan text names a CloudWatch alarm / log metric / on-call owner for the mcp daemon's health or the /mcp edge
findings.finding: The plan stands up a new always-on prod HTTP daemon (the `mcp` compose service) and a new blue-green autodeploy target, but names no health/liveness CloudWatch alarm or log-based monitoring for the mcp service itself — only a 'retention/cap/alert' on retired releases. The repo already establishes a per-service monitoring convention (monitoring_foxterrier.tf, monitoring_autodeploy.tf, monitoring_*.tf), so a new prod service with no named alarm is an observability gap.
findings.location: Decomposition items 2 (cibophobic-holohedral-esok) and 3 (panicky-sylphish-foxterrier); design summary 'Autodeploy' bullet ('retention/cap/alert')
scenarios: The rebar-mcp container crash-loops or the nginx /mcp/ upstream serves 502 in prod and no alarm fires — clients silently lose the dogfooded MCP path until a human notices
A blue-green cutover leaves the green container unhealthy and the retire-when-idle alert (scoped to retention) does not cover an outright liveness failure of the active release
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the esok or foxterrier slice a monitoring_mcp.tf (mirroring monitoring_foxterrier.tf) that alarms on mcp container health / nginx /mcp/ upstream failures to the existing /rebar/prod/alert-endpoint, and state the owner.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign explicit ownership (avians/9015 or esok/fd4a) with an acceptance oracle for materializing /rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key from SSM to the mcp container's bind-mount, since b173's container signing depends on it and no current child's ACs cover it.
evidence: b173: 'the materialized Ed25519 key, fetched from SSM /rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key by infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh to the bind-mount the container reads'
9015 scope: 'fetch-secrets.sh materializes each per-client PAT from SSM into ... .env as MCP_CLIENT_PAT_{COPILOT,CODEX,CLAUDE}, and emits the tokens JSON' — opcert-ed25519-key never mentioned
9015 ACs: guard / materialize (MCP_CLIENT_PAT_*) / verifier / runbook — no opcert key oracle
findings.finding: Dependency gap: no child's acceptance criteria own materializing the opcert Ed25519 signing key onto the box for the mcp container. b173 states the key is 'fetched from SSM /rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key by infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh to the bind-mount the container reads', but avians (9015) — the secrets/fetch-secrets.sh owner — scopes only the per-client MCP_CLIENT_PAT_* materialization; its ACs never mention the opcert-ed25519-key. b173 itself only lands the in-process signer-binding code and defers/assumes the key delivery.
scenarios: The mcp container boots with REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key but no child materialized that file to the box, so the bind-mount source is missing (the beb1 directory failure) and signing breaks — undermining b173 AC1 in production.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend 9015's fetch-secrets.sh materialization scope + an AC to cover the opcert-ed25519-key SSM→bind-mount delivery (or explicitly note it is pre-existing on the box and cite where), so b173's signing path has an owned key source.
